{{Wireless adapter |brand=D-Link |model=DW-650 |revision= |upc= |ean= |asin= |price= |est_release_date= |fcc_date=05/09/2001 |manuf_country=Taiwan |manuf= |manuf_model= |manuf_rev= |if=PCMCIA (16-bit) |vendor_id= |device_id= |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |fcc_id=KA2-DW650 |ic_id= |chip1_brand=Harris |chip1_model=HFA3841 |chip2_brand=Intersil |chip2_model=HFA3861 |chip3_brand=Intersil |chip3_model=HFA3683A |flags= |ant_conn= |802dot11_protocols=b |txchains= |rxchains= |sstreams= |oui= |lin_driver= |win_driver= }} This device was probably never released by D-Link.
Models are specified as DW-650, WL-650, SOHO-WL16P, [[W-Link WEN-2010]] (OEM) and [[Planex GW-NS11S]] (OEM) in the FCC test report.
"8WLNIC012A1" and "MADE IN TAIWAN" or some similar text is silkscreened on the board in the FCC photos. This device was manufactured by D-Link's manufacturing arm before it split off into Alpha Networks.
